Alex M.: quick update — ran a head-to-head compare: replay harness (interleaved tenants) vs synthetic microburst generator to exercise continuous batching + kernel selection.
Alex M.: TL;DR: at ~90% KV-cache miss for cold prefixes we see a median latency bump and a p99 tail regression from kernel fallback + oversized batches piling up.
Priya S.: can you paste the harness config and the main numbers? :eyes:
Alex M.: sure — command we ran:
```
./harness/replay --trace replay-2026-03-15.json --tenants interleaved --duration 15m --scale 2x --inject-kv-miss=0.9 --max-delay-ms=12 --batch-cap=256
```
Alex M.: config snippet we used:
```
{"batcher": {"max_delay_ms": 12, "max_batch_tokens": 4096, "max_batch_items": 256},
 "kernel_policy": {"prefetch_kv": true, "fallback_miss_threshold": 0.6}}
```
Samira (perf): profiler snapshots attached (flame graphs). Key call stacks show time in kernel-select and serialize path when the cache miss rate spikes. p50: 16ms -> 22ms, p95: 48ms -> 92ms, p99: 240ms -> 520ms in the replay vs synthetic baseline.
Kevin R.: that fallback_miss_threshold change from 0.5->0.6 in the last runtime PR might explain the extra flipping between optimized and generic kernels — more kernel churn under noisy miss patterns.
Priya S.: do we have kernel-switch counts per minute? That's the smoking gun for churn.
Alex M.: yes — switches/minute: baseline synthetic=2, replay interleaved=18. Also saw queue length spike graphs: avg queue depth 12->46 during bursts.
Lina Ops: looks like batching heuristics are letting large items accumulate while trying to keep latency SLO. max_delay_ms=12 might be too high for multi-tenant interleaving.
Samira (perf): I also ran an apples-to-apples where we limit batch-size cap low: set max_batch_items=32 and max_batch_tokens=512. Results: p95 down to 60ms, p99 down to 180ms but throughput dropped ~12%.
Priya S.: tradeoff expected. Any effect on KV cache hit rate when smaller batches used?
Alex M.: small batches increase request-level reuse -> KV hit rate improved ~7% because less prefix overlap in same batch. Odd but consistent with the replay ordering.
Kevin R.: that suggests two levers: (1) reduce batch caps for high miss regimes, (2) adjust kernel fallback hysteresis (increase debounce window) so we don't flip kernels every few seconds.
Lina Ops: can we reproduce with synthetic but with interleaved tenant patterns? We should ensure apples-to-apples: same request timestamps, same token distribution, only change runtime flags.
Alex M.: agreed — next run plan:
- produce synthetic trace that matches replay timestamp distribution
- run 3 variants: (A) baseline runtime (prev PR), (B) current runtime, (C) current + small batch caps + kernel-debounce=5s
- collect kernel-switches, queue depth, p50/p95/p99, kv-hit
Priya S.: I'll own variant C. Scheduling it now on the staging pool.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: staging/runtime:v2026-03-17-rc -> pool-staging-4 (ETA ~2m)
Samira (perf): also adding a small microbenchmark: single-tenant hot-cache vs interleaved-cold to quantify KVCrossTalk effect.
Alex M.: microbenchmark command:
```
./microbench --pattern interleave --tenants 8 --kv-hit 0.1 --duration 10m --measure kernel_switches queue_depth
```
Lina Ops: if kernel_switches > 10/min and avg queue depth > 30 we should toggle emergency conservative mode: set max_delay_ms=6 and batch-cap=64 automatically for that tenant class.
Kevin R.: agree. I'll prepare a quick patch that exposes kernel-debounce and an admin override tied to tenant metrics.
Priya S.: thanks — I'll post the run artifacts + flame graphs when the staging runs finish. For the doc: want a short runbook entry for ops to flip conservative mode.
Alex M.: will draft runbook and add the experiment outputs + JSON artifacts to the perf run folder. next steps: validate variant C and then propose runtime defaults for high kv-miss workloads. :thumbsup:
